headline: Debutant Morris beats Rock and explains tinnitus earplugs
standfirst: Tommy Morris averaged 100.33 in a 5-2 win over Josh Rock on his Grand Slam debut and spoke about wearing earplugs on stage.
body: Tommy Morris began his Grand Slam of Darts debut with a surprise 5-2 win over Josh Rock in Wolverhampton on Saturday afternoon, averaging 100.33.
After the match he spoke about the hearing problems he has lived with. Morris said he has had tinnitus for about three years, which he describes as ringing or buzzing in the ears.

To cope on stage he wears Loop earplugs, having asked the PDC for permission to use them. He likened them to "really good earbuds", and said they reduce the noise around him so he can concentrate on the board.
That includes the crowd. Morris said he zones out and that supporters "can whistle all you want" without it reaching him.
The win is a strong opening for a player new to the event, and in a format where only the group winner goes through, beating a seed first-up is valuable.
